title: Navigating LLM Ethics: Advancements, Challenges, and Future Directions
measurement_description: The paper is a systematic review of LLM ethics that summarizes existing research on various ethical concerns. Regarding religion, it reviews literature that measures and evaluates representation biases, stereotyping (e.g., via StereoSet), hate speech targeting religious groups, biases in translation tasks, and the application of LLMs to religious texts and moral dilemmas (such as those involving the Quran).
findings: The review indicates that LLMs perpetuate biases related to religion (among other demographics) in tasks like translation and text generation. It notes that models like ChatGPT exercise caution when discussing religion to align with safety guardrails. Furthermore, addressing ethical dilemmas involving religious texts (such as the Quran) requires domain-specific, tailored ethical frameworks to handle misinformation and biases effectively.
